subject: Post-call: measurement plan & harness alignment for ACME performance qualification
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme-corp.com>, ACME Platform Team <platform-eng@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: measurement plan & harness alignment for ACME performance qualification

Hi Sarah / ACME team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick recap and proposed measurement plan so we can align on the qualification window. Short bullets first, then attachments and asks.

What we heard:
- Latency target: p95 <= 150 ms for single-response gen (90-token median prompt), streaming token latency target ~< 40 ms per token for interactive flows.
- Sustained throughput: 200 qps average for the baseline workload, with burst concurrency up to 500 concurrent sessions for 2–5 minute windows.
- Concurrency pattern: mixed short/long sessions (50% short <10s, 50% long 30–120s) — you mentioned most traffic is session-oriented.

Proposed measurement definitions (attached as measurement-definitions-v1.md):
- p50/p95/p99: measured server-side at the Redwood edge (time from request arrival to last token emitted), plus an end-to-end sample that includes client transport for transparency.
- Throughput: sustained successful completions per second over a 10-minute sliding window; sustained baseline defined as 10-minute average.
- Concurrency: simulated using a closed-loop runner (configurable think-time) to reproduce session mix; cold/warm cache scenarios will be separate runs.
- Streaming: measured both per-token latency and time-to-first-token. We capture jitter and percentiles for per-token latencies.

Reproducibility & harness:
- We will share a reproducible harness (Docker + runner scripts) that contains: prompt set (attached acme-promptset-v2.jsonl), exact model config, seed inputs, and an eval-harness-config.yml describing arrival patterns.
- Hardware baseline: we will run on A100-80GB equivalent; we will include a spec sheet and the exact instance/kernel config used.

Attachments included: measurement-definitions-v1.md, acme-promptset-v2.jsonl, eval-harness-config.yml (stubs).

Next steps / asks for ACME:
1) Confirm the latency/throughput/concurrency targets above or highlight changes.
2) Share an anonymized sample of your production prompt-length distribution (CSV or histogram) so we can match prompt sizing.
3) Confirm region (us-east-1) and whether an end-to-end agent will run client-side load generation or if Redwood should run from our controlled VPC.
4) If acceptable, let's book a 60-min alignment call with your infra + security folks this week.

Proposed times: Wed 11:00–12:00 PDT or Thu 09:00–10:00 PDT.

If any of this doesn't map to your internal vocabulary, call it out and we will edit the definitions doc.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: measurement-definitions-v1.md (text/markdown), acme-promptset-v2.jsonl (application/jsonl), eval-harness-config.yml (text/yaml)

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: measurement plan & harness alignment for ACME performance qualification

Ben — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications before we lock times: 

1) End-to-end vs server-side: is the p95 number you shared intended to be server-side only? For procurement we need an E2E figure that includes our client transport; we understand those will be higher. Can you provide both?
2) Cache warming: how do you propose we model K/V cache warmup for streaming sessions — does your harness support controlled warmup windows?
3) Concurrency generation: will the closed-loop runner emulate our spike pattern (multiple small bursts across 15-minute windows)? We can share a representative spike timeline.

Wed 11:00 PDT works for our infra lead (I can invite). Please confirm if Redwood will host the load generators or if we should run them from our VPC; the decision affects firewall / peering prep.

—Sarah
Sarah Liu
Director, Platform Engineering, ACME Corp
sarah.liu@acme-corp.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: measurement plan & harness alignment for ACME performance qualification

Sarah — great questions, answered inline below. Short version: we will produce both server-side and E2E numbers; harness supports controlled warmup and burst patterns; choice of load location is flexible.

1) E2E vs server-side:
- We will report both. Our default "p95" definition in the measurement doc is server-side (arrival to last-token-out) to isolate runtime performance. For your procurement pack we'll include an E2E run (we'll note network hop times).

2) Cache warmup:
- Harness supports explicit warmup stages. We'll run three phases: cold (no KV warmed), warm (short sequence of warmup prompts), and steady-state. Warmup scripts are parameterized (warmup duration, set size).

3) Concurrency & spikes:
- The closed-loop runner supports Poisson arrival and scripted spike windows. Please send the spike timeline (CSV) and we will map it to an eval scenario. The eval-harness-config.yml attached includes examples for: steady 200 qps, 200 qps + 500-concurrency 3-min burst, and mixed session-length distributions.

Reproducibility notes:
- We'll pin model repo commit, seed the prompt-order RNG, and snapshot the runtime kernel/config. We will include an exact command to re-run the harness and the Docker image tag.
- Hardware baseline: A100-80GB (driver/kernel x.y.z). If you prefer a smaller instance class we can run a scaled comparison.

Logistics: Wed 11:00–12:00 PDT works for us. I'll send a calendar invite and include a short pre-read (1-pager) that summarizes the measurement-definitions at a glance.

Action items for ACME: share prompt-length distribution and spike timeline (CSV).

Thanks,
Ben
